daily.brief: 過去兩日（14日晚到16日凌晨）有598則帖、155個帳號。最熱鬧的是$NVDA，188則帖裡看淡帳號明顯多過看好（26對8），但有人反駁估值比較。最乾淨的多頭是AMD、NBIS、SNDK，各有3-4個帳號一致看好。MSTR則有3個帳號明確看淡，點出Saylor的比特幣成本平均約75,500美元，目前持倉虧損。
daily.full:
共識

AMD有4個帳號一致看好，13則帖。@daniel_koss說越想越清楚我們將獲得像$AMD這樣的新冠軍和贏家。原帖。@stevehou指Anthropic是Nvidia餘波的主要贏家，最少鎖定Nvidia，在Google TPU、Amazon Trainium和AMD上作為可互換池運行。原帖。

NBIS有3個帳號看好，17則帖。@daniel_koss為它辯護，區分論點被證明錯誤的持倉，與論點正在實現但價格下跌（因糟糕宏觀、Jensen恐慌及僅一季失望）的情況，認為關鍵指標發展極佳。原帖。@ACInvestorBlog看到MACD正面背離，與先前見底模式一致，一直在累積股份。原帖。@JonahLupton認為無論開放、封閉或混合模型贏家，NBIS都會表現良好。原帖。

SNDK也有3個帳號看好。@zephyr_z9從價格為40美元時就一直看好NAND，現在問題是KV緩存卸載採用緩慢，超大規模雲端建設定製解決方案。原帖。@InvestmentGuru_說它是AI存儲的NAND閃存，需求隨AI基礎設施上升，本週進行8比1股票拆分。原帖。

APP有3個帳號看好。@CKCapitalxx引用它是一隻400美元的股票，交易價格315美元。原帖。@rubicon59認為CTO強烈暗示新Axin 3廣告放置模型是生成類型，相比Axon 2有更優放置準確度。原帖。

共同看淡

MSTR有3個帳號明確看淡，7則帖。@zeroshorts稱「$MSTR宏觀悲劇」，經過6年比特幣投資，Michael Saylor損失約102億美元，成本平均為75,500美元，比特幣目前交易價低於該成本平均15.8%。原帖。@biancoresearch指Strategy的平均購買價格為75,820美元，遠高於目前價格，目前持倉虧損約10,000美元。原帖。@rcwhalen提到比特幣跌至67,000美元，Schiff警告崩潰。原帖。

SMMT有2個帳號看淡。@adamfeuerstein報告FDA拒絕Summit Therapeutics的肺癌治療ivonescimab。原帖。@JacobPlieth指CRL震驚，在沒有OS益處的情況下有效性的實質證據未確立。原帖。

分歧

NVDA是絕對主角，188則帖，看好8個帳號、看淡26個。@munster_gene回應日益增長的敘事指NVDA有下行風險因為MU以4倍CY27盈利交易vs NVIDIA 10倍，兩者因AI基建上漲，但街頭預期美光有遺漏。原帖。@damnang2認為機率接近零，但如果黃仁勳成為台積電下任執行長，會把所有資金投入NVIDIA。原帖。看淡聲音仍明顯較多。

SPCX偏多但有交鋒，21個看好對2個看淡，69則帖。@FirstSquawk指SpaceX創造歷史，Starship安全從軌道返回並完成著陸機動。原帖。@Dillon_Valdez說史詩般的一天已經到來，感謝SpaceX極其有才華的團隊。原帖。

MU有3對1，21則帖。@JonahLupton說DRAM價格在第四季可能再上漲12-15%，明年20-30%，好奇是否會看到SK Hynix或美光的運營利潤率達到84-85%。原帖。@InvestmentGuru_指記憶體是AI的安靜瓶頸，MU向短缺銷售DRAM和NAND。原帖。

其他值得留意

RKLB有2個帳號看好，擁有太空競賽的一份，從發射公司轉向太空基礎設施。CBRS、CSCO、LLY各有2個看好。整體AI相關鏈和太空名字有多頭，但大票分歧明顯。

weekly.full:

AMD在這週持續獲看好，14個帳號明確支持，零看淡。AMAT 9個、RKLB 4個、SNDK、NU、ONDS等也有多個帳號站在多頭。整體AI相關芯片和太空名字有較強共識。

MSTR有明確看淡，IWM、SMCI、GLD、SMMT等也有2-3個帳號負面。部分指數和商品有較一致的負面看法。

分歧

NVDA 188則帖中看淡帳號多過看好（26對8），有人反駁與MU的估值比較。SPCX獲21個帳號共識看好，Starship成功著陸被點名。MSTR有3個帳號明確看淡，點出Saylor比特幣成本平均約75,500-75,820美元，目前持倉虧損。

AMD、NBIS、SNDK各有3-4個帳號共識看好。一週和一個月來看，AMD共識較強，大市和AI龍頭則持續分歧。

daily.brief: Over the past two days (evening of the 14th to early morning of the 16th) there were 598 posts from 155 accounts. The busiest was $NVDA, with 188 posts where bearish accounts clearly outnumber bullish ones (26 vs 8), though some push back on valuation comparisons. The cleanest longs are AMD, NBIS, and SNDK, each with 3-4 accounts in agreement. MSTR has 3 accounts clearly bearish, pointing out Saylor’s Bitcoin cost average around $75,500, with current holdings in loss.
daily.full:
Consensus

AMD has 4 accounts in agreement, 13 posts. @daniel_koss says the more he thinks about it, the clearer it is that we will get new champions and winners like $AMD. original post. @stevehou notes Anthropic is the main winner of the Nvidia aftershock, the least locked into Nvidia, running on Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, and AMD as interchangeable pools. original post.

NBIS has 3 bullish accounts, 17 posts. @daniel_koss defends it, distinguishing positions where the thesis was proven wrong from cases where the thesis is playing out but the price is down (due to bad macro, Jensen panic, and only one disappointing quarter), saying key metrics are developing extremely well. original post. @ACInvestorBlog sees positive divergence on MACD, consistent with prior bottoming patterns, and has been accumulating shares. original post. @JonahLupton believes NBIS will do well whether the winner is open, closed, or hybrid models. original post.

SNDK also has 3 bullish accounts. @zephyr_z9 has been bullish on NAND since the price was $40; the issue now is slow KV cache offload adoption as hyperscalers build custom solutions. original post. @InvestmentGuru_ says it is the NAND flash for AI storage, demand rising with AI infrastructure, with an 8-for-1 split this week. original post.

APP has 3 bullish accounts. @CKCapitalxx cites it as a $400 stock trading at $315. original post. @rubicon59 believes the CTO strongly implies the new Axin 3 ad placement model is generative type, with better placement accuracy than Axon 2. original post.

Joint Bearish

MSTR has 3 accounts clearly bearish, 7 posts. @zeroshorts calls it “$MSTR macro tragedy”: after 6 years of Bitcoin investment, Michael Saylor lost about $10.2 billion, cost average $75,500, Bitcoin currently trading 15.8% below that average. original post. @biancoresearch notes Strategy’s average purchase price is $75,820, far above the current price, with holdings currently down about $10,000. original post. @rcwhalen mentions Bitcoin fell to $67,000, Schiff warning of collapse. original post.

SMMT has 2 bearish accounts. @adamfeuerstein reports the FDA rejected Summit Therapeutics’ lung cancer treatment ivonescimab. original post. @JacobPlieth says the CRL is shocking: substantial evidence of effectiveness not established without OS benefit. original post.

Divergence

NVDA is the absolute protagonist with 188 posts, 8 bullish and 26 bearish accounts. @munster_gene responds to the growing narrative of NVDA downside risk because MU trades at 4x CY27 earnings vs NVIDIA 10x; both rose on AI infrastructure, but there are omissions in street expectations for Micron. original post. @damnang2 thinks the probability is near zero, but if Jensen Huang becomes the next TSMC CEO, he would put all money into NVIDIA. original post. Bearish voices are still clearly more numerous.

SPCX leans bullish with some back-and-forth, 21 vs 2, 69 posts. @FirstSquawk says SpaceX made history, Starship safely returned from orbit and completed the landing maneuver. original post. @Dillon_Valdez says an epic day has arrived, thanks to SpaceX’s extremely talented team. original post.

MU has 3 vs 1, 21 posts. @JonahLupton says DRAM prices may rise another 12-15% in Q4, 20-30% next year, wondering if we will see SK Hynix or Micron operating margins reach 84-85%. original post. @InvestmentGuru_ says memory is AI’s quiet bottleneck; MU sells DRAM and NAND into the shortage. original post.

Other Noteworthy

RKLB has 2 bullish accounts, owning a piece of the space race, shifting from launch company to space infrastructure. CBRS, CSCO, LLY each have 2 bullish. Overall AI-related chains and space names have longs, but large names show clear divergence.
daily.html:
Short Summary

NVDA 188 posts with more bearish than bullish accounts (26 vs 8); MSTR has 3 accounts clearly bearish, pointing out Saylor’s cost average around $75,500. AMD, NBIS, SNDK each have 3-4 accounts in consensus bullish. 598 posts from 155 accounts.

weekly.brief: Over the past 7 days (Nov 10 to 16) there were 1765 posts from 241 accounts. AMD remains the clearest consensus bullish with 14 accounts and zero bearish. AMAT and RKLB also have support. NVDA is still the biggest hotspot but split, with more bearish. MSTR is a clearer bearish name.
weekly.full:
Consensus

AMD continued to be favored this week, 14 accounts clearly supportive with zero bearish. AMAT 9, RKLB 4, SNDK, NU, ONDS etc. also have multiple accounts on the long side. Overall AI-related chips and space names have stronger consensus.

Joint Bearish

MSTR has clear bearish views; IWM, SMCI, GLD, SMMT etc. also have 2-3 accounts negative. Some indices and commodities have more consistent negative views.

Divergence

NVDA remains the biggest split. SPCX leans bullish; CBRS, SPY, CSCO, TSLA, NBIS, QQQ all have back-and-forth. Some see the AI capex story unchanged; others worry about near-term events and valuation.

Other Noteworthy

The AI and space themes continue, but near-term sentiment is interrupted by individual company news.

monthly.brief: Over the past 28 days (Oct 20 to Nov 16) there were 6127 posts from 290 accounts, the largest discussion volume. AMD, SOFI etc. have stronger consensus bullish; RDDT has multiple accounts bearish. Large names NVDA, SPCX, SPY are heavily split. The AI theme remains central, but individual company events and valuation divergences are clear.

briefing.html:
Today's Highlights

NVDA 188 posts with more bearish accounts than bullish (26 vs 8); some push back on the valuation comparison with MU. SPCX has consensus bullish from 21 accounts; Starship successful landing is noted. MSTR has 3 accounts clearly bearish, pointing out Saylor’s Bitcoin cost average around $75,500-75,820, with current holdings in loss.

AMD, NBIS, SNDK each have 3-4 accounts in consensus bullish. Looking at the week and month, AMD consensus is stronger, while the broad market and AI leaders continue to diverge.
